hindi: माना $A$ तथा $B$ ऐसे परिमित समुच्चय हैं कि $n(A)=5$, $n(B)=7$ तथा $n\big((A\times B)\cup(B\times A)\big)=54$, जहाँ $n(X)$ परिमित समुच्चय $X$ के अवयवों की संख्या को दर्शाता है। तब $n\big((A\cup B)\times(A\cap B)\big)$ बराबर है
solution: A pair lies in both products iff both its entries lie in $A\cap B$: $(A\times B)\cap(B\times A)=(A\cap B)\times(A\cap B)$. With $k=n(A\cap B)$:
solution_full: For finite sets $n(X\times Y)=n(X)\,n(Y)$, so $n(A\times B)=5\cdot7=35$ and $n(B\times A)=7\cdot5=35$.

An ordered pair $(x,y)$ lies in $A\times B$ and in $B\times A$ exactly when $x\in A$, $y\in B$, $x\in B$ and $y\in A$, that is, when $x\in A\cap B$ and $y\in A\cap B$. Hence $(A\times B)\cap(B\times A)=(A\cap B)\times(A\cap B)$.
Let $k=n(A\cap B)$. Then $n\big((A\times B)\cap(B\times A)\big)=k^{2}$ and, by the formula for the number of elements of a union,
$n\big((A\cup B)\times(A\cap B)\big)=8\cdot4=32$. (The value $28$ comes from using $n(B)$ in place of $n(A\cup B)$, and $36$ from taking $n(A\cup B)=9$.)
originality_note: New: the size of the intersection is recovered from the union of a Cartesian product with its reversed product, via (AxB) n (BxA) = (AnB)x(AnB) used in reverse (way 5: Cartesian product structure linked with the counting formula). Closest known: NCERT-type exercise 'A and B have 3 elements in common, n(A)=3, n(B)=4; find n((AxB)n(BxA))'. Different because: the union count is given and the common part has to be solved for as a perfect square, then used in a new product.
